title: Finding FB2-REV-FND-000033: the class-A void*-identity failures had THREE causes, not one; a content-comparison recipe applied blindly is wrong for two of the three
lifecycle_status_note: 'draft': measured root causes with a demonstrated test-side remediation applied to 10 of 14 tests, verified by a full before/after host sweep with zero regressions. Four tests remain red and are reported as not fixable without changing what they assert. No human reviewer has confirmed the analysis; human approval remains 'pending'. This record makes no MISRA conformance claim, no tool-qualification claim and no certification claim of any kind.

revision_history.author: verification_engineer
revision_history.description: First record. Supersedes the single-cause framing of FB2-REV-FND-000031 with a three-way classification, each case backed by a decisive experiment rather than by inference.

evidence: FB2-REV-FND-000031 classified all 14 remaining class-A failures as one mechanism, 'identity silently downgraded an intended content comparison', and prescribed one recipe: a CMock callback doing TEST_ASSERT_EQUAL_MEMORY over the real sizeof. THAT RECIPE IS CORRECT FOR ONLY SOME OF THEM. Applying it as prescribed to tests/unit/app/application/bal/history/test_bal_strategy_history.c did NOT make the test pass. It failed with 'Memory Mismatch. Byte 12 Expected 0x00 Was 0x01'. Byte 12 of DATA_BLOCK_BALANCING_CONTROL_s is 'bool enableBalancing' (database_cfg.h:316-329, header then enableBalancing at offset 12), and the test itself sets that field to true two lines earlier at test_bal_strategy_history.c:101. The two objects therefore differ BY DESIGN and a content comparison is the wrong oracle. THE DECISIVE EXPERIMENT: in that test 'bms_tableControl' appears at exactly two places, test_bal_strategy_history.c:90 (its declaration) and :103-104 (the two _ExpectAndReturn arguments) and nowhere else. It is a dead decoy: the code under test never receives it. The test instead holds the real object via 'TEST_BAL_GetBalancingControl()' (:100), which returns '&bal_balancing' (bal_strategy_history.c:397-399), and BAL_Init (bal.c:146-152) passes its argument straight through via DATA_READ_DATA/DATA_WRITE_DATA. Replacing the two decoy arguments with 'pBalancing' - changing nothing else - and deleting the now-unused decoy (which the compiler then flagged under -Werror=unused-variable, independently confirming it had been dead) yields TESTED 3 / PASSED 3 / FAILED 0. Identity was NEVER a silent downgrade there; identity was the CORRECT oracle and the test passed the WRONG POINTER. The same shape was then found and fixed the same way in test_bal_strategy_voltage.c (3/3) and test_debug_default.c (11/11), the latter proven non-vacuous by swapping two of the four expected pointers and observing 'Expected 0x0000000100068058 Was 0x0000000100068000'. THE THREE-WAY CLASSIFICATION, each case established by reading the call site and the fixture rather than by assumption. (A) PROPAGATION, 3 tests: the test holds the real object and passed a decoy - test_bal_strategy_history.c:103, test_bal_strategy_voltage.c:101, test_debug_default.c:245. Identity is correct and achievable; the fix strengthens the test, because it now asserts that the driver propagates the caller's block, which nothing asserted before. (B) REACHABLE STATIC, UNMUTATED AT THE CALL SITE, 4 tests: the block is a function-local or file-scope static of the product translation unit that the test cannot address, and it still holds its initial value, so a full content comparison is both possible and meaningful - test_interlock.c:210/265/279 (ilck_tableAdcVoltages, read at interlock.c:215 before anything writes it), test_moving_average.c:135 (read at moving_average.c:195), test_database.c (16 assertion sites), test_debug_default.c is case A not B. (C) MUTATED BEFORE PUBLISH, 7 tests: the product fills the block in before publishing it, so a full content comparison is impossible and only the header identity is meaningful - test_state_estimation.c:116/123/129/135 (SE_Initialize* mutates then writes at state_estimation.c:79-80, :85-86, :91-92, :96-100), test_soc_lookup-table.c:114, test_nxp_mc33775a_i2c.c, and the two can_cbs_rx_imd_bender-iso165c tests. A SECOND ORDER FINDING, only visible once the comparison was made field-wise rather than by raw bytes: DATA_QUEUE_MESSAGE_s has 4 bytes of STRUCT PADDING between 'accessType' (offset 0, 4 bytes) and 'pDatabaseEntry' (offset 8), measured with offsetof against the repository's own headers: offsetof(accessType)=0, sizeof(accessType field)=4, offsetof(pDatabaseEntry)=8, sizeof=40. Production initialises it with a designated initialiser (database.c:150-155) which does not write the padding, so those bytes are indeterminate on the product side and zero in the test's file-scope object. A raw TEST_ASSERT_EQUAL_MEMORY over sizeof(DATA_QUEUE_MESSAGE_s) therefore fails at 'Byte 4' for reasons that have nothing to do with the data the queue carries. The product's CAN_BUFFER_ELEMENT_s and the N77X AFE_I2C_QUEUE_s fixtures have the same property: their test fixtures are designated initialisers leaving readData[], writeData[], registerAddress and readDataLength uninitialised. Comparing those field-wise is not a weakening, it is the only comparison the fixtures support. SIZE EVIDENCE, measured not assumed, with a standalone probe compiled against the repository headers: DATA_BLOCK_SOC_s 32, DATA_BLOCK_MIN_MAX_s 52, DATA_BLOCK_MOVING_AVERAGE_s 60, DATA_BLOCK_BALANCING_CONTROL_s 112, DATA_BLOCK_CELL_VOLTAGE_s 88, DATA_BLOCK_ADC_VOLTAGE_s 140, DATA_QUEUE_MESSAGE_s 40, CAN_BUFFER_ELEMENT_s 24, CAN_CAN2AFE_CELL_TEMPERATURES_QUEUE_s 20, CAN_CAN2AFE_CELL_VOLTAGES_QUEUE_s 14. NON-VACUITY, one bit flipped per recipe: test_interlock.c 'Memory Mismatch. Byte 14 Expected 0x80 Was 0x00'; test_database.c 'Expected 0 Was 1'; test_soc_lookup-table.c 'Expected 36 Was 27'; test_can_cbs_rx_imd_bender-iso165c-info.c 'Memory Mismatch. Byte 12 Expected 0x01 Was 0x00'. Each was reverted. WEAKENING CHECK, applied to every replacement: a CMock '_Stub' returns BEFORE CMock's own argument, call-count, strict-ordering and return-value checks (Mockio.c:462-468 and the same shape in every generated mock), so it is weaker than the '_ExpectAndReturn' it replaces. Every callback used here therefore re-establishes them explicitly - a per-block step counter pins the call count and the inter-call order, the return value is asserted against what the test declared, and '_CallCount()' is asserted at the end of the test so 'called fewer times than expected' is caught - which is why the recipe used here is STRICTLY STRONGER than the one applied to test_diag_cfg.c in FB2-REV-FND-000031, not weaker.
impact: Acting on the single-cause framing of FB2-REV-FND-000031 as written would have been actively harmful in case (A). Prescribing 'compare the content' for test_bal_strategy_history.c produces 'Memory Mismatch. Byte 12' - a failure that looks like a product defect and is not one - and leaves the test red, while the one-line correct fix (pass the pointer the test already holds) is never discovered. The cost of getting this wrong is not merely wasted work: a reviewer who saw 'Byte 12 Expected 0x00 Was 0x01' on a balancing-control struct and no stack trace could reasonably conclude that BAL_Init corrupts the enableBalancing flag, and go looking for a bug in safety-relevant balancing logic that does not exist. The coverage gain is real and measured: 10 of the 14 tests now carry a working oracle where they previously carried an assertion that could never pass, taking the suite from 196 pass / 17 fail to 208 pass / 5 fail with zero regressions. The remaining cost is that 4 tests still have no working oracle. The limit of what is demonstrated must be stated plainly: every fix here is TEST-SIDE, and a passing test under this harness says nothing about register-map correctness, timing, clocking, interrupts, DMA transfer, bus or electrical behaviour, device identity, or EMAC/MDIO descriptor semantics. A SIL harness that mocks the HAL verifies driver logic against upstream's own pre-existing assertions; it does not verify the device. Nothing in this record is evidence of MISRA conformance, of tool qualification, or of any certification, and no such claim may be inferred from it.
root_cause: One framing was applied to three different situations, and the recipe that fits one of them was prescribed for all three. The common precondition is real and unchanged: CMock cannot size a void*, so :when_ptr: :compare_data degrades to UNITY_TEST_ASSERT_EQUAL_PTR (cmock_generator_utils.rb:207-210, with the in-source comment that void* cannot be safely dereferenced and there is no way to specify depth without the array plugin), and an identity comparison can never hold when the two sides hold different objects. What differs is WHY they hold different objects, and that determines what the correct assertion is. In case (A) the test holds the real object and simply named the wrong one: the expectation was satisfiable all along and the test was passing a dead decoy, so the fix is to pass the real pointer and the assertion becomes a genuine propagation check. In case (B) the real object is genuinely unreachable - a private static of the product translation unit - so identity is impossible, and because the block is still unmutated at the call site, content over the real sizeof is achievable and is what the fixture's field-by-field declaration was asking for. In case (C) the real object is unreachable AND already mutated by the time it is published, so neither identity nor full content is achievable; only the header identity, which is the field that actually records which database entry was published, is both meaningful and stable. A fourth situation, found while doing this, is that some of these structs contain struct padding or fixture members that no side initialises, which makes a raw byte comparison unsound independently of everything above and requires a field-wise comparison. The prior framing missed all of this because it never opened the failing tests to ask what the fixture was for, and inferred intent from the fixture's declaration comment alone.
resolution: PARTIALLY RESOLVED, deliberately. Resolved and green, each verified by running the test: case (A) test_bal_strategy_history.c 3/3, test_bal_strategy_voltage.c 3/3, test_debug_default.c 11/11 - all three now pass the real pointer, which strengthens rather than weakens them, and in test_debug_default.c three dead 'Compare' fixtures were confirmed to be decoys rather than the published blocks. Case (B) test_interlock.c 11/11 and test_moving_average.c 1/1 compare the unmutated block by content over the real sizeof; test_database.c 14/14 compares field-wise because of the padding, and additionally re-asserts the queue handle by IDENTITY and the timeout, both of which are correct because 'ftsk_databaseQueue' is the same extern object on both sides. Case (C) test_state_estimation.c 5/5, test_soc_lookup-table.c 6/6, test_can_cbs_rx_imd_bender-iso165c-info.c 15/15 and test_can_cbs_rx_imd_bender-iso165c-response.c 10/10 assert the header identity plus, where the fixture supports it, a field-wise content comparison. test_soc_lookup-table.c additionally had a genuine independent test defect fixed: its 'cp_pTableMinMax' was declared DATA_BLOCK_SOC_s (32 bytes) while the product reads DATA_BLOCK_MIN_MAX_s (52 bytes), so it could not have been a content comparison of the right type either; the fixture now has the correct type. No file under src/ was modified. Every recipe is proven non-vacuous by a one-bit flip with the failure captured, and every deliberate change was reverted. NOT RESOLVED, four tests, left red on purpose. test_debug_can.c (3 assertions), test_can_cbs_rx_afe_cell-temperatures.c (1) and test_can_cbs_rx_afe_cell-voltages.c (1): the test passes a uint64_t where the product passes a 20-byte CAN_CAN2AFE_CELL_TEMPERATURES_QUEUE_s or a 14-byte CAN_CAN2AFE_CELL_VOLTAGES_QUEUE_s, and the test never reads the buffer back. Identity is impossible; content is undefined and would read past the end of the test's own object; there is no uniqueId because these are not database blocks. Proven, not assumed: retyping the decoy to the product's actual type STILL fails, so this is not a typing slip. There is no correct oracle and fixing it would require either a correctly typed local the test does not have or a redesign of what it asserts. test_nxp_mc33775a_i2c.c (7 assertions): the same out-parameter situation, but the posted request also carries a per-branch completion code that the product derives from mocked SPI results, and the product rewrites 'module' and 'transferType' between construction and posting (nxp_mc33775a_i2c.c:292-295, :384, :394, :406, :419). Working out the correct per-site expectation required reading five separate product branches; an attempt was made, was abandoned as it was becoming a guess at product semantics rather than a test fix, and was fully reverted - the file is byte-identical to HEAD and its result is unchanged at 3 pass / 7 fail. These 4 are reported as defects, not worked around. Also still open and unaffected: the conf/unit CMock configuration defect on the by-value uint64_t parameter, now fixed in the SIL harness configuration and recorded separately as FB2-REV-FND-000034; and the test_dp83869.c segfault, now root-caused and recorded separately as FB2-REV-FND-000035.
